verses.text: Now when all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah, and broke the pillars in pieces, cut down the Asherah poles, and broke down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, also in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the children of Israel returned, every man to his possession, into their own cities.

Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites after their divisions, every man according to his service, both the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to minister, to give thanks, and to praise in the gates of Yahweh’s camp.

He also appointed the king’s portion of his posessions for the burnt offerings, for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths, for the new moons, and for the set feasts, as it is written in Yahweh’s law.
Moreover he commanded the people who lived in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might give themselves to Yahweh’s law.

As soon as the commandment went out, the children of Israel gave in abundance the first fruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and of all the increase of the field; and they brought in the tithe of all things abundantly.

The children of Israel and Judah, who lived in the cities of Judah, also brought in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of dedicated things which were consecrated to Yahweh their God, and laid them in heaps.
In the third month they began to lay the foundation of the heaps, and finished them in the seventh month.
When Hezekiah and the princes came and saw the heaps, they blessed Yahweh and his people Israel.
Then Hezekiah questioned the priests and the Levites about the heaps.

Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, answered him and said, “Since people began to bring the offerings into Yahweh’s house, we have eaten and had enough, and have plenty left over, for Yahweh has blessed his people; and that which is left is this great store.”
Then Hezekiah commanded them to prepare rooms in Yahweh’s house, and they prepared them.
They brought in the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things faithfully. Conaniah the Levite was ruler over them, and Shimei his brother was second.

Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah were overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of God’s house.
Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the porter at the east gate, was over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute Yahweh’s offerings and the most holy things.

Under him were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in their office of trust, to give to their brothers by divisions, to the great as well as to the small;

besides those who were listed by genealogy of males, from three years old and upward, even everyone who entered into Yahweh’s house, as the duty of every day required, for their service in their offices according to their divisions;
and those who were listed by genealogy of the priests by their fathers’ houses, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their offices by their divisions;

and those who were listed by genealogy of all their little ones, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, through all the congregation; for in their office of trust they sanctified themselves in holiness.

Also for the sons of Aaron the priests, who were in the fields of the suburbs of their cities, in every city, there were men who were mentioned by name, to give portions to all the males among the priests, and to all who were listed by genealogy among the Levites.
Hezekiah did so throughout all Judah; and he did that which was good, right, and faithful before Yahweh his God.
In every work that he began in the service of God’s house, in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he did it with all his heart, and prospered.

footnotes.content: See how the revival spreads like clean water through the land—not just words, but shovels in hand, breaking what's false. All Israel moves as one body: the priests lead, the people follow, and even the old high places come tumbling down. That's the kind of faithfulness the Lord prizes: the whole people, together, turning home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hezekiah doesn't leave it to chance—he appoints divisions, settles each priest and Levite into their work with the Lord's house at the center. Notice: their service is *for* thanksgiving and praise. Not grudging duty, but gladness. Structure serves grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The king opens his own purse—morning, evening, Sabbath, new moons, all the holy times. Not because the law demands it, but because he sees it written and *builds it into his life*. A leader's giving sets the tone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hezekiah commands Jerusalem to *provide* for the priests and Levites so they can *give themselves to God's law*. Generosity creates room for others to grow deep in the Lord. It's an act of love for the servants of His house.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word goes out and abundance follows—grain, wine, oil, honey, the earth's own increase. In the biblical witness, generosity *itself* is a sign of God's presence. Israel hears the call and answers with open hands, giving the first and the best.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They bring cattle, sheep, and offerings 'consecrated to the Lord,' laying them in heaps. See the faith here—they give what is *holy*, set apart already for God. That kind of giving comes from hearts that recognize everything belongs to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Third month to seventh month—four months of gathering and piling up. It's patient work, steady work, the kind that takes time and trust. The heaps grow and grow. Generosity, once released, has its own momentum.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: King and princes come to *see* with their own eyes—and they bless the Lord and His people. Sometimes leadership means witnessing grace at work and speaking it aloud. That blessing spoken in public becomes a wound of thanksgiving in the whole nation's heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hezekiah *asks*—he doesn't assume. He goes to the priests and Levites and wants to understand the heaps, the work, the outpouring. A humble king listens first. That's how you learn where grace is moving.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Azariah the chief priest speaks witness: *'We have eaten and had enough, and have plenty left over, for the Lord has blessed His people.'* There is the mark of true revival—abundance that nourishes *and* overflows. That 'great store' is the visible sign of God's hand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now Hezekiah commands storerooms to be built. The abundance is so real, so fruitful, that *infrastructure* must follow. When revival comes, even your buildings have to change shape to hold it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Conaniah and Shimei serve as rulers over the offerings—faithful work that keeps the house of God in order. Notice: *'faithfully.'* The great gifts come in because ordinary people do ordinary work with a whole heart. That faithfulness matters as much as the abundance.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ten names—Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, and the rest—overseers appointed by the king and the high priest. These are the hands-on people who turned the king's vision into daily work. Revival runs on the shoulders of faithful servants whose names the Lord knows.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Kore stands at the east gate, keeper of freewill offerings—the *most holy things*. Not by chance is he at the entrance; he is guardian of the threshold where the people's devotion flows into God's house. Such work is the sacred choreography of a people coming home to their Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Six assistants serve under Kore—Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, Shecaniah—distributing portions to their brothers great and small. Notice the *smallness* honored alongside the great. In the Lord's house, every one matters, every name is known.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the little ones—from three years old—are listed and counted, each assigned their duty according to their divisions. Hezekiah's renewal reaches into the smallest corners; the Lord's house welcomes and includes the young from the very start.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Priests and Levites—listed by genealogy, by age, by their fathers' houses—all have their place in the order. Structure and identity matter; each person knows who they are and where they serve. The Lord's family is built on such solid knowing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Little ones, wives, sons, daughters—*the whole family*—all sanctified in holiness through their office of trust. Hezekiah's revival reaches across generations and genders. That's how grace works: it transforms not just the individual, but the *household of God*.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In the suburbs, in the fields—even outside the city walls—men are appointed to give portions to priests and Levites. Grace reaches *everywhere*, not just the temple center. The Lord's care for His servants extends into the quiet corners too.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hezekiah did this *throughout all Judah*—not halfway, not in the capital alone, but everywhere. And what he did was *good, right, and faithful before the Lord*. That's the measure: does it please God? Does it serve His people? Hezekiah kept his eyes on that north star.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo in Hezekiah's wholehearted seeking: *'he did it with all his heart, and prospered.'* The Lord honors the undivided heart. In a scattered age, when we pull ourselves in a thousand directions, there's a quiet wisdom here—that singular devotion still opens heaven's doors, and still brings blessing to those around us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
